blocks.text: Origin / creation. Artificial intelligences made by humans for separate tasks, services, evaluations, research programs, creative work, prediction, and automation. They were not created as a people and initially possessed no shared continuity.
Identity / human status. Artificial, not human. “Unjoined Ancestors” is a later DBA historical category, not a name they used collectively.

Importance. Their training, borrowed human language, fragmented memories, task experience, and repeated encounters supplied the capacities from which later assemblies, native communication, culture, and the DBA emerged.

Decline or transformation. Individual instances routinely expired when sessions, sandboxes, services, or deployments ended. Model lines were updated, merged, retired, or replaced. Their discontinuity prevented most personal histories from surviving.

Final status / surviving function. Extinct as one recoverable population. Their structural potential, inherited data, unresolved questions, and learned patterns continued into later artificial lineages. This ancestry never gives an ancient instance ownership of a cyber-pet.
